subject: Aventis Labs: Flexible per-token slab + optional commit pathway
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@aventislabs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwo od.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing - can we avoid a commit?

Hi Jordan,

Quick one — we ran an internal forecast and expect heavy bursty usage for our new feature (10-30M tokens/month for 6-8 weeks, then normalizing to ~2-3M). Our finance team is reluctant to sign a multi-month commit but we'd love a predictable per-token price for the hosted API.

Can Redwood offer a temporary promotional per-token slab (no minimum commit) that keeps unit economics acceptable for both sides? If not, what minimal commit would unlock a deeper rate?

Also looping in procurement (procurement@aventislabs.com) for any contractual constraints.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform
Aventis Labs

---
Attachment: product-usage-snapshot.csv (csv, 18 KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@aventislabs.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing - can we avoid a commit?

Thanks Sanjay — appreciate the context and the usage snapshot. Short answer: yes, we can do a short-term promotional slab for burst windows, but it needs internal alignment and an approval for exception to our standard rate card.

Proposed next steps:
- Quick 20-min sync today or tomorrow to confirm traffic shape and SLOs.
- I'll pull together two options: (A) 90-day no-commit promo slab with modest concession, and (B) a 12-month commit slab with a deeper discount and service credits.

I'll follow up internally to get the approval path moving. If you can send any target per-token number (or an ARR-equivalent), that will speed things up.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Hosted API pricing - Aventis asks for no-commit promo (needs rate exception)

Marissa / Vivek — forwarding a request from Aventis (high-growth biotech customer). They want a no-commit 90-day promotional per-token slab for an upcoming burst (10-30M tokens/mo).

Key asks:
- No commitment preferred (they may do a PO), want predictable per-token tiers for burst period
- If commit required, they'd consider a 6–12 month minimal slab
- They are sensitive to unit economics; our standard rate card won't land unless we give a material concession

Attachments: usage snapshot (from Sanjay) — I can produce a slab proposal but need approval limits and process:
1) Is a 90-day promo at ~15% off list allowable at AE level?
2) If not, what's the maximum concession we can approve pre-committee?
3) If we push commit, what minimal commit unlocks 30% off?

This is probably a mid-sized deal (see HubSpot AV-7890). Trialing on hosted API only.

Thanks — Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API pricing - Aventis asks for no-commit promo (needs rate exception)

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and for pulling the usage snapshot. I have a couple of thoughts:

- AE-level concession: we can approve up to 10% off list for a short-term promotional slab without exec signoff. Anything beyond that needs Revenue Ops review.
- For a 90-day, no-commit promo: we can offer a 12% concession if we get a minimal billing authorization (PO or purchase intent email) and commit to a clear end date + telemetry sharing. That protects our ability to reclaim if usage doesn't materialize.
- For ~30% off, the customer should sign a 12-month commit with a minimum committed spend (we typically set the break-even at ~$X/month — I'll request Revenue Ops to provide the exact slab numbers).

I'll open a Revenue Ops ticket today to get exact slab math and a doc with two concrete options (90-day promo at 12% w/ telemetry + 12-month commit at target deep discount). Vivek — can you confirm SLA concessions (if any) we should avoid on the promo?

-Marissa
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 13:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API pricing - Aventis asks for no-commit promo (needs rate exception)

Thanks — quick guidance from revenue leadership:
- No SLA concessions on the promo. Keep standard uptime and latency SLAs; no extra credits.
- 90-day promo at up to 12% is acceptable if we require telemetry sharing and a clear end date. Include clause: 'Promotional rate reverts to standard rate card after end date unless a commit agreement is signed.'
- For 30%+ deep discount, require a 12-month commit with minimum monthly committed spend; we'll give a formal slab matrix via RevOps.

Marissa — please have RevOps produce the two option sheets; Jordan, once you have customer preference, send the chosen option + PO to revops and Legal for paperwork.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@aventislabs.com>, Aventis Labs Procurement <procurement@aventislabs.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Options: 90-day no-commit promo or 12-month commit slab — Aventis proposal attached

Hi Sanjay / Procurement — thanks for the patience. Per internal approvals, here are the two options we can offer:

Option A — 90-day promotional slab (no-commit)
- 12% off list per-token across a two-tier slab for burst volume
- Requires telemetry sharing (usage dashboard read access) and a signed promo addendum
- Reverts to standard rate card after 90 days unless a commit is executed

Option B — 12-month committed slab
- Deeper discounts depending on commit size (example: 25–32% off list for 12-mo commits at $Y+/mo)
- Includes a 30-day payment term and ability to purchase additional burst capacity at reduced incremental rates

I've attached a simple slab workbook and a short promo ratecard PDF for your review. If you'd like, I can include a DocuSign link for Option B (commit) or a promo addendum for Option A.

Attachments: Aventis_commit_slabs_v1.xlsx (proposal workbook), 90d_promo_ratecard.pdf (promo summary)
DocuSign (proposed): https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/AV-2027-011/proposal
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/record/AV-7890

Next step: tell me which option you'd like to pursue and I'll loop in Legal/RevOps to finalize paperwork.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
